content: Common failure modes are false precision, hidden fallback output, success status that masks poor inputs, and automation that silently changes a reviewed value. The safer product contract is to reject or flag unsupported inputs, label estimates and provider quality separately from accuracy, preserve model and review history, show a human veto path, and fail safely when the provider is unavailable. On low-end CPU hardware, the product should prefer a bounded, reviewable result over a photorealistic digital twin or a cloud/GPU-only promise. The project context further rules out fabricated accuracy percentages, public body assets, and treating the deterministic local fallback as personalized production measurement. Sources: https://www.styku.com/en-us/support-kb/why-are-my-scan-measurements-inaccurate-even-though-the-scan-completes-successfully ; https://www.nist.gov/pml/nist-technical-note-1297/nist-tn-1297-7-reporting-uncertainty ; https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/airmf/5-sec-core/
